status_summary: On 2025-03-12 the EPA Administrator announced that EPA would reevaluate its 2023 heavy-duty nitrogen oxide final rule, according to the later proposal. On 2026-07-14 EPA published a proposed rule for model year 2027 and later heavy-duty engines that does not reopen the NOx, particulate, hydrocarbon and carbon monoxide standards but would keep model year 2026 warranty periods, delay the longer useful life periods to model year 2030, create nonconformance penalties for certain diesel engines, and replace engine power derates with visible or audible notifications for urea system inducements. EPA estimated warranty savings of up to 6,000 dollars per diesel vehicle. EPA held virtual public hearings on 2026-07-29 and 2026-07-30, comments closed 2026-08-29, and no final rule was found in the Federal Register through 2026-10-25.

timeline.event: EPA published a proposed rule amending compliance provisions, warranty and useful life periods, nonconformance penalties and inducement rules for model year 2027 and later heavy-duty engines.
EPA held virtual public hearings on the proposal on 2026-07-29 and 2026-07-30, per the EPA rule page.

title: Reconsider the heavy-duty truck NOx rule to cut cost and compliance burden
uncertainties: The proposal leaves the numeric NOx standards intact, so alignment with the document is on cost and burden only. Federal Register API queries on 2026-10-25 (EPA, heavy-duty engines, nonconformance penalties, since 2026-07-15) found no final rule; the EPA rule page and an industry trade report of 2026-10-07 (docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2026-0728) both describe the proposal as still pending, with no stated final-rule date. The trade report states that if the amendments are not finalized, the 2023 rule's model year 2027 requirements apply from 2027-01-01. A final action could still appear before model year 2027 production. Two announcements were moved out of the timeline on 2026-10-25 because announcements are not counted as events: the Administrator's 2025-03-12 statement that EPA would reevaluate the 2023 rule (as recounted in the proposal) and EPA's 2026-07-09 announcement of the proposal (Transport Topics); both remain in sources.
